coverage.evidence: overlay/mlx/backend/omarchy/primitives.cpp:6569-6585 selects QmmTileRbF16 only when the tile path is enabled, RB is enabled, output/input dtype is float16, transpose_ is true, bits_ == 4, and group_size_ == 64. The 32-row by 16-column dispatch at lines 6575-6583 matches the shader tile.

overlay/mlx/backend/omarchy/shaders/qmm_tile.comp:57-67 defines TILE_M=32, ROWS_PER_THREAD=4, W_ROWS_PER_THREAD=2, and a 16x8 workgroup. Static enumeration showed each shared-X row 0..31 and each shared-weight row 0..15 has exactly one writer. The baseline macro branch still maps rows 0..15 and weight rows 0..15 exactly once.

qmm_tile.comp:307-389 matches the transposed affine addressing in qmm.comp:325-370: words_per_row=K*bits/32, parameter index column*(K/group)+k/group, packed word column*words_per_row+k/pack, and low-bit-first lane extraction. Each output accumulator still visits k in ascending order.

qmm_tile.comp:206-222 computes ceil(M/32), ceil(N/16), and grid-strides both axes. Lines 236-243 zero-fill out-of-range M/K loads; lines 249-250 guard N and non-transposed K; lines 405-412 guard final M/N stores. For the selected transposed group-64 path, the validated shape makes K a multiple of 64 and therefore 16, so no K tail exists.

qmm_tile.comp:394 places a barrier after all tile_x/tile_w writes; line 403 places a barrier after all consumers finish and before the next K tile can overwrite shared storage. Both barriers execute under uniform loop control.

CMakeLists.txt:252 builds qmm_tile_rb_f16 with USE_FP16 and REGISTER_BLOCK; compute.h:539-542 appends QmmTileRbF16 before Count; compute.cpp:265 includes the generated header and lines 1163-1164 return its bytes. The enum append preserves prior kernel IDs.

test_matmul_family.cpp:2816-2914 enables the exact candidate and compares it with both the baseline tile and a host reference. Cases 32x32x128 and 33x17x64 cover a full tile and simultaneous M/N tails; finite checks prevent NaN/Inf false passes; candidate and baseline are required to be bit-identical.

coverage_gaps: The register-block-specific test does not directly exercise M<32, batched weights, or dispatch-clamped grid-stride iteration. Source analysis found the same guards and indexing cover these cases, so this is not a proven defect.
